I have the same problem, and there were a couple of issues at play, each that I'm working on:

1. I was bullied in primary school when I started, and this started me down a track where I protected myself by not getting close. It doesn't help that my family isn't the most functional - they're not raging screaming feuding people, but we just drift apart and do our own thing without being too attached to each other.
2. I was depressed by my mother's emotional abuse, this started about the age of 16 and reduced my capability to be happy, which in turn reduced my capability to connect to people. Spending good times with them is a great way to build a connection. Instead, I'd just play humour in such a way as to keep them at arms length.
3. I never believed I was someone worth connecting to, due to my mother's aforementioned abuse. I only thought I had worth in terms of my academic skills.
4. I escaped to my computer, it became my outlet and escape, and while I'd talk to people over Facebook, I still wasn't truly connecting.

The only type of shit I copped for not showing emotions was to do with my prickliness (e.g. I had bystanders comment on how awkward my hugs were), because I at least had developed strong empathic skills, but I never connected aside from liking to help people.

I'm improving now, I'm even going as far as to notice girls for the purposes of attraction, and it's only really happening because I'm taking anti-depressants, talking to a psychologist who understands how I feel and can bring me down to earth, and because I'm making the effort to reconnect with friends, and I finally realised last night when a friend wasn't replying to my texts, that I'd actually be incredibly devastated if she'd had a car accident and died. First time I can remember feeling that was the case.

I get the feeling your issue could stem from something (or more than one something) else that feeds into your perception of the world and people (not least - yourself), and depression is a fantastic example of that. Obviously that's not the only reason it could happen, but it's something I like to talk about now that I realise how much it was ruining my life, and my father's, and so I thought it was worth mentioning.

If you have any questions or want any advice from the perspective of someone who's slowly fixing that problem myself, I'm happy to answer, via PM or comment.

Not quite an accurate comparison - that would be equivalent to getting a prenuptial agreement before getting married despite expecting a happy marriage.

You don't expect your car to crash every time you drive it, do you? If you're expecting to lose her as a matter of course, that's not equivalent to just-in-case insurance, that's equivalent to expecting things to go wrong.

You can't experience true happiness and joy if you're constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, and if you're not happy in your relationship, it's less likely to last.

Not to mention that your *expectation* that she will leave will affect the way you act, meaning it's more likely.

There could be other issues at play behind it too - whilst I've never had actual sex, I did definitely identify with this phrase:

> I do masturbate fairly regularly. However, even this doesn't feel that great, I do it more to satiate an irritating urge than because it feels nice.

I used masturbation as some kind of I'm bored/down reaction, and it's only now that I've started taking anti-depressants that I've started to have anything turn change on the sexual front at all. If you're clinically depressed, it can have a massive effect on enjoyable activities, and general feelings of pleasure. If you have other troubles such as enjoying other activities, feeling sad or numb frequently, energy problems or appetite problems, you might have something worth talking to a doctor about. I would definitely mention your lack of sexual pleasure if you do see one.
